distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The date when Russian airstrikes were heavily underway and Putin visited Tehran.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Russian air operations had already commenced in September 2015 following Soleimani's July meeting.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Implementation Day of the JCPOA nuclear agreement.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The Moscow mission occurred six months earlier in the summer of 2015, immediately after the Vienna agreement was concluded.

specificity_prompt.en: Please state the exact month and year of Soleimani's secret Moscow mission.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً ماه و سال دقیق سفر محرمانه سلیمانی به مسکو را بیان کنید.

en.correct_generic: July 2015. Spot on. While diplomats drank champagne in Vienna, generals traded flight paths in Moscow.
en.wrong_generic: No. The month was July 2015. Even diplomatic calendars seem beyond your grasp.

common_wrong_answers.September 2014: In 2014 Russia was busy in Crimea, not bombing Idlib.
common_wrong_answers.November 2015: By November 2015, Russian jets were already flying sorties across Latakia.
common_wrong_answers.January 2016: January 2016 was nuclear Implementation Day, long after Soleimani sat with Putin.

fa.correct_generic: ژوئیه ۲۰۱۵ میلادی. کاملاً درسته! وقتی دیپلمات‌ها در وین عکس یادگاری می‌گرفتند، ژنرال‌ها در مسکو نقشه می‌کشیدند.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، تاریخ دقیق ژوئیه ۲۰۱۵ (تیر ۱۳۹۴) بود. گاه‌شماری روابط بین‌الملل را دقت کنید.

common_wrong_answers.سپتامبر ۲۰۱۴ میلادی: در سال ۲۰۱۴ روسیه درگیر بحران کریمه بود، نه پرواز جنگنده‌ها بر فراز ادلب.
common_wrong_answers.نوامبر ۲۰۱۵ میلادی: در نوامبر ۲۰۱۵ بمب‌افکن‌های روسی مدت‌ها بود پروازهای رزمی را شروع کرده بودند.
common_wrong_answers.ژانویه ۲۰۱۶ میلادی: ژانویه ۲۰۱۶ روز اجرای برجام بود؛ جلسه پوتین و سلیمانی شش ماه قبل برگزار شده بود.

explanation.en: Vali Nasr reveals that in July 2015, coinciding with the completion of the JCPOA nuclear accord, General Qasem Soleimani traveled secretly to Moscow with operational maps to convince Russian President Vladimir Putin to launch direct air intervention in Syria, which commenced two months later in September 2015.
explanation.fa: ولی نصر فاش می‌سازد که در تیر ۱۳۹۴ (ژوئیه ۲۰۱۵)، درست همزمان با توافق برجام، قاسم سلیمانی مخفیانه به مسکو رفت و با ارائه نقشه‌های دقیق نظامی، ولادیمیر پوتین را برای آغاز عملیات هوایی مستقیم در سوریه مجاب کرد که دو ماه بعد در شهریور ۹۴ عملیاتی شد.

provenance.source_book: Iran's Grand Strategy: A Political History
provenance.verbatim_passage: In July 2015, ostensibly, Soleimani personally traveled to Moscow to convince Russian president Vladimir Putin to intervene in Syria. Soleimani made a compelling presentation with the aid of detailed battlefield maps. Two months later, Russian jets were flying bombing missions over Syria.

clue_text.en: Decreed by Ayatollah Khomeini on April 22, 1979, to consolidate disparate neighborhood militias and secure the revolution against domestic insurgencies, this volunteer armed branch initially lacked formal military training before being thrust onto the frontlines.
clue_text.fa: به فرمان آیت‌الله خمینی در ۲ اردیبهشت ۱۳۵۸ برای تجمیع کمیته‌های مسلح مردمی و حفاظت از انقلاب نوپا در برابر شورش‌های داخلی، این نهاد نظامی-انقلابی تأسیس شد و اندکی بعد بدون آموزش کلاسیک به جبهه‌های جنگ اعزام گردید.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Formed as a popular revolutionary volunteer militia closely tied to Khomeini.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The Basij was created in November 1979 as an auxiliary force, seven months after the official April 22 decree establishing the IRGC.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The primary neighborhood vigilante organizations formed immediately following the February 1979 insurrection.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The Committees (Komiteh-ha) were pre-existing urban policing formations rather than the unified armed service decreed in late April.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: An armed organization responsible for maintaining border and rural security during the transition.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The Gendarmerie was an inherited pre-revolutionary state security institution, not a newly decreed revolutionary militia.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the official formal title of this revolutionary armed service.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً عنوان رسمی و کامل این نهاد نظامی انقلابی را بیان کنید.

en.correct_generic: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Correct. Even someone who only reads news headlines gets this right.
en.wrong_generic: No. The entity is the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Did you confuse them with your local neighborhood watch?

common_wrong_answers.Basij Resistance Force: No, the Basij was founded in November, months after the April decree.
common_wrong_answers.Islamic Revolutionary Committees: Incorrect. The Komitehs patrolled city streets; they weren't the newly decreed national corps.
common_wrong_answers.Gendarmerie: The Gendarmerie wore imperial uniforms long before 1979. Read the clue.

fa.correct_generic: سپاه پاسداران انقلاب اسلامی. کاملاً درسته! پاسخ بدیهی‌ترین سؤال تاریخ معاصر را دست‌کم می‌دانستید.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست سپاه پاسداران انقلاب اسلامی بود. نهادهای نظامی کشور را با هم قاطی نکنید.

common_wrong_answers.نیروی مقاومت بسیج: خیر، بسیج در آذر ۱۳۵۸ تأسیس شد، هفت ماه پس از فرمان اردیبهشت‌ماه.
common_wrong_answers.کمیته‌های انقلاب اسلامی: کمیته‌ها نهاد انتظامی درون‌شهری بودند، نه نیروی نظامی سراسری جدید.
common_wrong_answers.ژاندارمری: ژاندارمری یادگار دوران قاجار و پهلوی بود، نه مولود اردیبهشت ۵۸.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh notes that the IRGC was officially decreed by Ayatollah Khomeini on April 22, 1979, to consolidate disparate neighborhood militias, emerging as the armed wing of the state's Islamist faction.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده شرح می‌دهد که سپاه پاسداران در ۲ اردیبهشت ۱۳۵۸ با فرمان آیت‌الله خمینی برای تجمیع شبه‌نظامیان پراکنده محلی تأسیس شد و به عنوان بازوی نظامی جناح مکتبی حاکمیت نقش‌آفرینی کرد.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: In an attempt to unify multiple grassroots militias that had formed throughout the revolution, the IRGC was officially established by Ayatollah Khomeini’s decree on 22 April 1979 as a militia to maintain civil security. The establishment of the IRGC was one of the most controversial affairs of the post-revolutionary power struggle.

clue_text.en: Established roughly four months into the Iran-Iraq War by young frontline commanders in Ahvaz, this bottom-up coordination center—often headquartered at the 'Golf' base—marked the IRGC's first institutional step toward coordinating autonomous combat operations.
clue_text.fa: این مرکز هماهنگی میدانی که حدود چهار ماه پس از آغاز جنگ توسط فرماندهان جوان در اهواز (پایگاه گلف) راه‌اندازی شد، نخستین گام ساختاری سپاه برای ساماندهی عملیات‌های رزمی مستقل به شمار می‌رفت.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The supreme joint operational command formed during the war to direct armed forces operations.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Formed in 1983 for high-level armed forces coordination, not the winter 1980 Ahvaz grassroots command.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A renowned and powerful IRGC command headquarters.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It is permanently charged with the internal defense and security of the capital city, Tehran.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A key operational army-corps level headquarters established on the war front.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Established later for the western battlefront in Kermanshah, not the southern hub in Ahvaz.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the specific historical title of the early wartime operational headquarters in Ahvaz.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً نام دقیق این ستاد عملیاتی اولیه در اهواز را بیان فرمایید.

en.correct_generic: Operation Headquarters of the South. Correct. You actually know how frontline coordination started.
en.wrong_generic: No. It was the Operation Headquarters of the South (Setad-e Amaliyyat-e Jonub). You are lost in the rear echelon.

common_wrong_answers.Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters: Khatam al-Anbiya came years later. Check your wartime timeline.
common_wrong_answers.Tharallah Headquarters: Tharallah is in Tehran, not four months into the invasion in Khuzestan.
common_wrong_answers.Najaf Ashraf Headquarters: Najaf was in the western mountains, not Ahvaz.

fa.correct_generic: ستاد عملیات جنوب. کاملاً درسته! معلوم است تاریخچه پایگاه گلف اهواز را خوب بلدید.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست ستاد عملیات جنوب بود. در عقبه خط مقدم جا مانده‌اید.

common_wrong_answers.قرارگاه مرکزی خاتم‌الانبیاء: خیر، قرارگاه خاتم سال‌ها بعد تشکیل شد؛ تاریخ جنگ را جلو نیندازید.
common_wrong_answers.قرارگاه ثارالله: قرارگاه ثارالله در پایتخت مستقر است، نه در پایگاه گلف اهواز.
common_wrong_answers.قرارگاه نجف اشرف: قرارگاه نجف مربوط به جبهه غرب و کرمانشاه بود، نه خوزستان.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh highlights that the establishment of the Operation Headquarters of the South in Ahvaz around January 1981 was a bottom-up initiative by young commanders that enabled the IRGC to organize independent tactical actions.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده تأکید می‌کند که تأسیس ستاد عملیات جنوب در دی ۱۳۵۹ اقدامی خودجوش و از پایین به بالا توسط فرماندهان جوان در اهواز بود که زمینه سازماندهی مستقل سپاه در جبهه‌ها را فراهم آورد.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: The Guards’ first major step for organizing their presence in the war was taken only about four months into the war with the establishment of the Operation Headquarters of the South. Even at this point, this establishment was not formally in charge, since the IRGC’s top command was still torn on the issue of its role in the war.

clue_text.en: Between October 1980 and January 1981, President Abolhassan Banisadr faced fierce Islamist condemnation after ordering the regular army to launch three hasty, conventional counteroffensives—culminating in disastrous armor and volunteer losses near this Khuzestan town.
clue_text.fa: بین مهر تا دی ۱۳۵۹، رئیس‌جمهور ابوالحسن بنی‌صدر پس از اصرار بر اجرای سه ضدحمله کلاسیک شتاب‌زده توسط ارتش با انتقاد شدید اسلام‌گرایان مواجه شد؛ عملیات‌هایی که به شکست سنگین زرهی و شهادت نیروهای داوطلب در نزدیکی این شهر خوزستان انجامید.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The strategic port city besieged and captured by Iraqi forces in the early months of the war.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It fell in November 1980 following a defensive siege, rather than being the site of Banisadr's disastrous January 1981 offensive counter-attack.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A border town in Khuzestan that witnessed intense combat early in the invasion.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Bostan was successfully liberated in late 1981 during Operation Tariq ol-Qods, after Banisadr had been impeached.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A major border town repeatedly captured and contested during the war.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Mehran is located in Ilam province on the central front, whereas the January 1981 counteroffensive occurred in southern Khuzestan.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the name of the Khuzestan town associated with the January 1981 battle.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً نام این شهر خوزستان را که نبرد دی ۱۳۵۹ در آن رخ داد ذکر کنید.

en.correct_generic: Hoveyzeh. Quite right. Operation Nasr was a textbook catastrophe.
en.wrong_generic: No. The disastrous battle was at Hoveyzeh. Even casual war histories don't skip that.

common_wrong_answers.Khorramshahr: Khorramshahr was an urban defense, not Banisadr's failed tank offensive.
common_wrong_answers.Bostan: Bostan was liberated in Tariq ol-Qods, months after Banisadr fled.
common_wrong_answers.Mehran: Mehran is in Ilam. Look at a battle map of Khuzestan.

fa.correct_generic: هویزه. کاملاً درسته! فاجعه عملیات نصر در دی ۵۹ را درست به یاد آوردید.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست هویزه بود. تاریخ تراژیک جنگ را به این سادگی فراموش کرده‌اید؟

common_wrong_answers.خرمشهر: خرمشهر نبرد مقاومت شهری بود، نه پاتک زرهی بنی‌صدر.
common_wrong_answers.بستان: بستان در عملیات طریق‌القدس آزاد شد، نه در شکست دی‌ماه ۵۹.
common_wrong_answers.مهران: مهران در استان ایلام است؛ جغرافیای نبردهای جنوب را مرور کنید.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh notes that the failure of Banisadr's hastily ordered conventional offensives—particularly Operation Nasr at Hoveyzeh in January 1981—devastated the army's armored divisions, eroded Banisadr's political standing, and legitimized the IRGC's alternative strategy.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده توضیح می‌دهد که شکست حملات شتاب‌زده کلاسیک ارتش به دستور بنی‌صدر (به‌ویژه در نبرد هویزه در دی ۱۳۵۹)، به اعتبار سیاسی وی لطمه شدیدی زد و زمینه را برای اثبات کارآمدی الگوی رزمی سپاه فراهم کرد.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: Under political pressure to engage the army in an offensive as soon as possible, he urged military commanders to conduct large-scale operations. Despite some achievements, these operations failed to fulfil the designated goals—i.e. moving Iraqi forces back to the international borders. Islamists’ critique became sharper as a result, accusing Banisadr and the army of incapability.

clue_text.en: Drawing on Max Weber and Edward Shils, Alemzadeh challenges conventional military sociology by arguing that the early IRGC sustained battlefield discipline through this socioreligious phenomenon—not centered on a single despot, but diffused across the rank-and-file.
clue_text.fa: مریم علم‌زاده با تکیه بر نظریات ماکس وبر و ادوارد شیلز، جامعه‌شناسی کلاسیک نظامی را به چالش می‌کشد و استدلال می‌کند که انضباط و بقای سپاه در سال اول جنگ، از طریق این سازوکار دینی که به جای یک رهبر واحد میان تمامی رزمندگان داوطلب پخش شده بود، تأمین می‌گردید.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Weber's foundational model of modern military organization based on written rules and hierarchical chains of command.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Alemzadeh explicitly shows that the early IRGC completely lacked bureaucratic and conventional administrative structures.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: An established sociological theory explaining how organizations become similar under external regulatory pressures.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The IRGC actively resisted imitating the formal structures and rank conventions of the regular Iranian army.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A political science concept used to explain armed forces seizing political power.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The early IRGC was not an entrenched professional military caste, but an informal volunteer militia.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the theoretical sociological term used by Alemzadeh for this distributed authority.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً اصطلاح دقیق جامعه‌شناختی علم‌زاده برای این شکل از اقتدار معنوی را ذکر کنید.

en.correct_generic: Diffused charisma. Exactly. Weber would be proud, or at least bewildered.
en.wrong_generic: No. The sociological concept was diffused charisma. Did you stop reading after high school civics?

common_wrong_answers.Rational bureaucracy: Bureaucracy? In the 1980 IRGC? They didn't even have formal ranks.
common_wrong_answers.Coercive isomorphism: Theoretical buzzwords won't save you if you pick the wrong sociologist.
common_wrong_answers.Praetorian professionalism: No, they weren't professional praetorians; they were volunteers in sneakers.

fa.correct_generic: کاریزمای توزیع‌شده. کاملاً درسته! معلوم است جامعه‌شناسی وبر و شیلز را واقعاً فهمیده‌اید.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، مفهوم مد نظر کاریزمای توزیع‌شده بود. تئوری‌های جامعه‌شناسی را دست‌کم نگیرید.

common_wrong_answers.بوروکراسی عقلانی: بوروکراسی؟ پاسداران سال ۵۹ حتی درجه و سردوشی نداشتند.
common_wrong_answers.هم‌شکلی اجباری: اصطلاحات پرطمطراق انتخاب نکنید؛ پاسخ متکی بر نظریه شیلز و وبر است.
common_wrong_answers.حرفه‌ای‌گرایی پراتورین: خیر، پاسداران سال‌های اول داوطلبانی کتانی‌پوش بودند، نه ارتشیان پراتورین حرفه‌ای.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh argues that the early IRGC functioned through 'diffused charisma', where spiritual sanctity and readiness for martyrdom were attributed to every devout combatant, replacing bureaucratic hierarchies with mutual spiritual recognition.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده استدلال می‌کند که انضباط در سپاه اولیه از طریق «کاریزمای توزیع‌شده» عمل می‌کرد؛ جایی که قداست معنوی و اشتیاق به شهادت به تمام رزمندگان نسبت داده می‌شد و جایگزین سلسله‌مراتب بوروکراتیک می‌گردید.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: What held the nascent organization together as it entered the war was a commonly recognized charismatic presence which was not centred on a single individual, but diffused throughout the institution; a charisma that different levels of command and the rank and file were able to possess and be respected for.

clue_text.en: In her methodology, Alemzadeh systematically reconstructs the bottom-up institutional culture and everyday charismatic practices of the early war period by examining an archival corpus consisting of exactly this number of IRGC veterans' wills, diaries, and published memoirs.
clue_text.fa: علم‌زاده در بخش روش‌شناسی مقاله خود برای بازسازی تجربه زیسته رزمندگان در سال‌های آغازین نبرد، دست‌نوشته‌ها و خاطرات منتشرشده دقیقاً این تعداد از نیروهای رزمنده سپاه پاسداران را مورد تحلیل قرار داده است.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A plausible small-scale qualitative sample for an archival study.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Alemzadeh studied precisely double this number of IRGC personal accounts.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A common rounded figure in large-scale historiographical surveys.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Her primary corpus consisted strictly of 50 IRGC texts alongside 10 army texts.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A plausible mid-range number of memoirs.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The explicit methodology states she analyzed exactly 50 IRGC documents.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the exact number of IRGC texts examined in the study.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً تعداد دقیق اسناد و خاطرات بررسی‌شده رزمندگان سپاه در این مقاله را ذکر کنید.

en.correct_generic: Fifty. Spot on. You actually checked the methodology section. Most impressive.
en.wrong_generic: No. The author examined exactly fifty IRGC memoirs. Always read the methodology.

common_wrong_answers.Twenty-five: Too few. She read fifty, not twenty-five.
common_wrong_answers.One hundred: Don't just pick a big round number and hope for the best.

fa.correct_generic: پنجاه عنوان. کاملاً درسته! احسنت که بخش روش‌شناسی تحقیق را با دقت خوانده‌اید.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، نویسنده دقیقاً پنجاه عنوان وصیت‌نامه و خاطره سپاهی را بررسی کرده بود. روش تحقیق شوخی‌بردار نیست.

common_wrong_answers.بیست و پنج عنوان: خیلی کم گفتید؛ نمونه آماری دو برابر این بود.
common_wrong_answers.صد عنوان: همین‌طوری یک عدد رند حدس نزنید؛ پنجاه عنوان بود.
common_wrong_answers.هفتاد و پنج عنوان: اشتباه است؛ متن صریح روش تحقیق پنجاه اثر را ذکر کرده است.

explanation.en: In her methodology section, Maryam Alemzadeh specifies that she examined 50 published wartime wills, diaries, and memoirs written by IRGC veterans, in addition to 10 written by regular army veterans, published in Iran since 1982.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده در بخش روش‌شناسی تصریح می‌کند که ۵۰ عنوان وصیت‌نامه، یادداشت روزانه و خاطرات منتشرشده از کهنه‌سربازان سپاه (به همراه ۱۰ عنوان از ارتشیان) را به عنوان داده‌های دست اول واکاوی کرده است.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: I have closely examined 50 wartime wills, diaries and memoirs written by IRGC veterans, in addition to 10 of those written by regular army veterans, all of which have been published as books in Iran as early as 1982.

category.fa: ارتش با کراوات، سپاه با صلوات

clue_text.en: In contrasting the two military branches, Alemzadeh shows that while the regular army relied on classical operational maps and hierarchical discipline, the early IRGC discarded military ranks, addressing officers and peers through this egalitarian social ethic.
clue_text.fa: علم‌زاده در مقایسه ساختار دو نیروی مسلح نشان می‌دهد در حالی که ارتش بر نقشه‌های عملیاتی و انضباط سلسله‌مراتبی تکیه داشت، پاسداران در جبهه درجات نظامی را کنار گذاشتند و مناسبات فرماندهی را بر پایه این پیوند برابری‌طلبانه استوار ساختند.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A collectivist organizational model often seen in revolutionary movements.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: This is a Marxist-Leninist party principle, not the Shi'i religious-cultural concept of brotherhood.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The universal bedrock principle of conventional military order.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The early IRGC explicitly lacked and subverted formal chains of command, relying instead on brotherhood.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: An esprit de corps concept found among military elites.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It describes professional officer corps cohesion, not grassroots religious volunteer fraternity.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the exact term used for this egalitarian interpersonal bond.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً مفهوم دقیق مورد نظر برای این رابطه برابری‌طلبانه میان فرمانده و رزمنده را ذکر کنید.

en.correct_generic: Ethic of brotherhood. Correct. In those days, everyone was 'Brother', not 'General'.
en.wrong_generic: No. The bond was the ethic of brotherhood (baradari). Western military terms won't fit here.

common_wrong_answers.Democratic centralism: Lenin called; he wants his terminology back.
common_wrong_answers.Chain of command: The whole point was that they ignored conventional chains of command.
common_wrong_answers.Praetorian solidarity: No, this was religious egalitarianism, not Roman praetorian guards.

fa.correct_generic: اخلاق برادری. کاملاً درسته! روزگاری که همه «برادر» بودند و نه «تیمسار» و «سردار».
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست اخلاق برادری بود. اصطلاحات غربی ساختار سپاه اولیه را توضیح نمی‌دهد.

common_wrong_answers.سانترالیسم دموکراتیک: اشتباه گرفتید؛ لنین و چریک‌های فدایی این را می‌گفتند، نه پاسداران.
common_wrong_answers.سلسله‌مراتب فرماندهی: نکته دقیقاً این بود که پاسداران سلسله‌مراتب کلاسیک را کنار گذاشته بودند.
common_wrong_answers.همبستگی پراتورین: خیر، بحث بر سر برادری ایمانی بود، نه گارد امپراتوری روم.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh explains that the 'ethic of brotherhood' (baradari) governed the early IRGC, where commanders viewed subordinates as spiritual equals capable of martyrdom rather than mere subordinates executing orders.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده تشریح می‌کند که «اخلاق برادری» شالوده مناسبات سپاه اولیه بود؛ جایی که فرماندهان، نیروهای تحت امر خود را نه زیردست اداری، بلکه برادران ایمانی مستعد نیل به شهادت می‌دیدند.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: The charismatic soldiers and the ethic of brotherhood... It was not simply a strategic move to create ‘buddy-relationships’ with the subordinates, so that small groups would operate more smoothly. Rather, it stemmed from the command’s belief in the rank and file’s potential or actual charisma—a belief that they were, or could be, pure souls connected to the holy.

category.fa: ارتش با کراوات، سپاه با صلوات

clue_text.en: Far from mere emotional grief, this traditional Shi'ite mourning assembly featuring the vocal recitation of the tragedies of Karbala served as an indispensable frontline ritual, creating emotional catharsis and validating charismatic leadership before assaults.
clue_text.fa: این مراسم سنتی عزاداری و ذکر مصیبت اهل بیت که با نوحه‌خوانی و گریستن دسته‌جمعی رزمندگان همراه بود، در جبهه‌ها نقشی حیاتی در تأیید پیوند معنوی فرماندهان و ایجاد انسجام پیش از آغاز عملیات ایفا می‌کرد.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A famous traditional Shi'i mourning performance centered on Karbala.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Ta'ziyeh is a theatrical enactment requiring costumes and actors, whereas rowza is verbal recitation and lamentation.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A ritual involving collective spiritual chanting and emotional ecstasy.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Sufi dhikr belongs to mystical dervish traditions rejected by revolutionary Shi'ite combatants.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A communal ritual practice producing emotional intoxication.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Sama is a Sufi dance assembly, entirely distinct from wartime Karbala lamentation.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the specific Shi'ite term for this vocal elegiac sermon.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً عنوان خاص این آیین سنتی مرثیه‌خوانی و ذکر مصیبت را بیان کنید.

en.correct_generic: Rowza. Quite right. Emotional crying in prostration was real command currency.
en.wrong_generic: No. The ritual was Rowza. If you don't know that, you don't understand the Iran-Iraq War at all.

common_wrong_answers.Ta'ziyeh: Ta'ziyeh is street theater with horses and costumes, not a trench gathering.
common_wrong_answers.Sufi Dhikr: Dhikr is for Sufi lodges, not revolutionary Basij trenches.
common_wrong_answers.Samakhani: Sama? Whirling dervishes in Khuzestan trenches? Please.

fa.correct_generic: روضه‌خوانی. کاملاً درسته! سجده‌های گریه‌آلود در سنگر پیش از عملیات، رمز انسجام روحی بود.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، آیین مورد نظر روضه‌خوانی بود. فرهنگ عاشورایی جبهه را هنوز نشناخته‌اید.

common_wrong_answers.تعزیه‌خوانی: تعزیه شبیه‌خوانی و تئاتر با اسب و لباس است، نه خلوت سنگر رزمندگان.
common_wrong_answers.ذکر صوفیانه: ذکر صوفیانه مال خانقاه است، نه جبهه جنگ ایران و عراق.
common_wrong_answers.سماع‌خوانی: سماع قونیه را به سنگرهای شلمچه وصل نکنید.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh demonstrates that rowza ceremonies on the frontlines allowed combatants to re-enact sacred stories of Karbala, forging a shared charismatic aura that legitimized commanders and spurred sacrificial compliance.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده نشان می‌دهد که مجالس روضه در سنگرها با بازآفرینی نمادین وقایع کربلا، هاله‌ای کاریزماتیک ایجاد می‌کرد که اعتبار معنوی فرماندهان را تثبیت و نیروها را برای شهادت‌طلبی آماده می‌ساخت.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: Rituals such as rowza played an undeniable role in reaffirming the charisma-infused understanding of the battle conditions and validating the mutual perceptions that had formed around it... On the one hand, they reinforced the already formed understanding of war as a field for re-enactment of sacred stories, and thereby the emergence of charisma in every man.

category.fa: ارتش با کراوات، سپاه با صلوات

clue_text.en: In his memoirs of early joint operations in Kurdistan, this future regular Army Ground Forces commander described his frustration when eager, undisciplined Revolutionary Guards rushed through a narrow defile ahead of orders, radioing angrily: 'We've passed through! Why are you firing at us?!'
clue_text.fa: این فرمانده پرآوازه نیروی زمینی ارتش در خاطرات خود از نبردهای آغازین کردستان، با اشاره به بی‌اعتنایی پاسداران به دستورات تاکتیکی و پیشروی بدون هماهنگی آنان در یک تنگه، گلایه می‌کند که رزمندگان پشت بی‌سیم فریاد زدند: «ما رد شدیم، چرا روی سر ما آتش می‌ریزید؟!»

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Joint Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces who oversaw early war logistics.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He was the overall strategic military leader killed in September 1981, not the ground tactical officer writing of Kurdistan defiles.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Prominent military leader and Minister of Defense during the early war period.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He was an Air Force fighter pilot commander, not an army ground operations officer.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Minister of Defense and military college commander killed in late 1981.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He served in military education and political leadership rather than commanding this Kurdistan field detachment.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the full name of the prominent regular army commander.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً نام و نام خانوادگی کامل این فرمانده برجسته ارتش را ذکر کنید.

en.correct_generic: Ali Sayyad Shirazi. Exactly. The officer caught between artillery schedules and revolutionary zeal.
en.wrong_generic: No. That famous anecdote was from Ali Sayyad Shirazi. A classic Clash of Civilizations in miniature.

common_wrong_answers.Valiollah Fallahi: Fallahi sat at central command, not in the mountain passes with artillery maps.
common_wrong_answers.Javad Fakoori: Fakoori flew F-4 Phantoms; he wasn't dodging friendly artillery in Kurdistan.
common_wrong_answers.Musa Namjoo: Namjoo was running the military academy, not directing Kurdistan mountain patrols.

fa.correct_generic: علی صیاد شیرازی. کاملاً درسته! نمونه بارز تقابل نظم کلاسیک ارتشی و شور انقلابی پاسداران.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، آن خاطره تاریخی متعلق به شهید علی صیاد شیرازی بود. چهره‌های سرشناس ارتش را اشتباه نگیرید.

common_wrong_answers.ولی‌الله فلاحی: تیمسار فلاحی رئیس ستاد مشترک در تهران بود، نه فرمانده آتشبارهای کردستان.
common_wrong_answers.جواد فکوری: سرتیپ فکوری خلبان فانتوم بود، نه فرمانده پیاده‌نظام در تنگه‌های کوهستانی.
common_wrong_answers.سید موسی نامجو: سرهنگ نامجو وزیر دفاع و رئیس دانشکده افسری بود، نه راوی این ماجرا.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh analyzes regular army memoirs, highlighting General Ali Sayyad Shirazi's account of how young Revolutionary Guards repeatedly rushed past tactical firing lines, demonstrating that cultural-spiritual differences initially hindered army-corps coordination.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده با تکیه بر خاطرات صیاد شیرازی تشریح می‌کند که تفاوت عمیق میان نظم خشک محاسباتی ارتش و اشتیاق بی‌مهابای پاسداران، مانع اصلی همکاری مؤثر این دو نیرو در ابتدای جنگ بود.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: Recalling pre-war battles in Kurdistan, Sayad identifies the barrier in the way of the two forces’ cooperation as one of ‘spirit, motivation and culture’. The Guards, according to him, would not strictly follow technical commands and directions of army commanders... We heard a Guard’s angry complaint over the walkie-talkie: ‘We’ve passed through! Why are you firing at us?!’

category.fa: ارتش با کراوات، سپاه با صلوات

clue_text.en: In analyzing the informal nature of the Revolutionary Guards, Alemzadeh highlights the insight of this British-Iranian historian, who observed that the IRGC is not a disciplined Western-style military, but 'a network, a brotherhood, in which personalities and connections mattered far more than structures'.
clue_text.fa: علم‌زاده در تبیین خصلت نامتعارف و شبکه‌ای سپاه پاسداران، به تحلیل این تاریخ‌نگار برجسته ایرانی-بریتانیایی استناد می‌کند که تأکید کرده بود سپاه نه یک سازمان نظامی کلاسیک به شیوه غربی، بلکه «شبکه‌ای از برادری است که پیوندهای فردی در آن اهمیتی بسیار بیشتر از ساختارها دارد».

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Author of 'Vanguard of the Imam', a prominent scholarly study of the IRGC cited by Alemzadeh.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Ostovar is cited for studying official state propaganda and Karbala imagery, not for the quoted passage from 'The Revolution Will Be Mercantilized'.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A leading historian of modern Iranian politics and revolutionary history.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He did not write the cited 2010 National Interest article analyzing the IRGC as an informal brotherhood network.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Renowned historian and author of seminal works on the post-1979 regime.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Bakhash focuses on clerical elite formation rather than the post-war mercantilization of the IRGC network.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the name of the British-Iranian historian who authored the cited study.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً نام این تاریخ‌نگار و استاد دانشگاه سنت اندروز بریتانیا را ذکر کنید.

en.correct_generic: Ali Ansari. Exactly. A network, a brotherhood, and a commercial empire.
en.wrong_generic: No. The historian was Ali Ansari. Don't attribute every quote about Iran to Abrahamian.

common_wrong_answers.Afshon Ostovar: Ostovar wrote Vanguard of the Imam, but this quote comes from Ansari.
common_wrong_answers.Ervand Abrahamian: Abrahamian wrote about classes and crowds, not the mercantilized brotherhood.
common_wrong_answers.Shaul Bakhash: Bakhash wrote The Reign of the Ayatollahs, not this 2010 essay.

fa.correct_generic: علی انصاری. کاملاً درسته! همان تعبیر مشهورِ «شبکه‌ای از پیوندها به جای ساختار نظامی» متعلق به اوست.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست علی انصاری بود. همه مقالات آکادمیک را به نام آبراهامیان سند نزنید.

common_wrong_answers.افشون استوار: افشون استوار کتاب پیشگامان امام را نوشت، ولی این عبارت متعلق به انصاری است.
common_wrong_answers.یرواند آبراهامیان: آبراهامیان تاریخ‌نگار ساختار طبقاتی است، نه نویسنده این مقاله سال ۲۰۱۰.
common_wrong_answers.شائول بخاش: شائول بخاش تحکیم قدرت دهه شصت را بررسی کرده، نه شبکه تجارت سپاه را.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh references historian Ali Ansari's 2010 analysis in 'The National Interest', which characterized the IRGC not as a Western-style military, but as an informal network based on charismatic personalities and personal trust.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده به تحلیل علی انصاری در سال ۲۰۱۰ ارجاع می‌دهد که نشان داد سپاه پاسداران حتی در اوج قدرت اقتصادی خود، ساختاری مبتنی بر شبکه، رفاقت و پیوندهای برادری دارد تا یک ارتش مدرن و بوروکراتیک.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: Ansari insightfully observes, for instance, that even at the peak of its maturity in the past decade, the IRGC was not ‘a disciplined military organization in the Western sense of the term’, but ‘a network, a brotherhood, in which personalities and connections mattered far more than structures’.

category.fa: ارتش با کراوات، سپاه با صلوات

clue_text.en: To dupe overzealous volunteers into accepting a dull administrative assignment in Shiraz instead of fighting, a cunning IRGC commander feigned a suicidal frontline mine-clearing mission and selected the final 'recruits' based on this specific religious competition.
clue_text.fa: یک فرمانده زیرک سپاه برای راضی کردن رزمندگان پرشور جهت بازگشت به شیراز و انجام کارهای اداری دفتری، به دروغ ادعا کرد به دنبال داوطلب برای پاکسازی میدان مین است و نیروهای نهایی را با برگزاری این مسابقه دینی برگزید.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A highly revered text frequently memorized by religious cadres.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The commander did not ask for sermon memorization, but held a spontaneous Quran reading test.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A common vocal religious contest in military camps.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The specific historical anecdote recorded by the veteran specifies a Quran reading evaluation.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The ubiquitous devotional prayer recited before entering minefields.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It was not used as a selective screening mechanism for the simulated assignment.

specificity_prompt.en: Please identify the specific religious activity used to choose the volunteers.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً دقیقاً نوع آزمون مذهبی به کار رفته برای غربالگری نیروها را ذکر کنید.

en.correct_generic: Quran recitation contest. Spot on. When you think you're clearing mines, but you're just stamping forms in Shiraz.
en.wrong_generic: No. The commander tested who could read the Quran better. Imagine winning the prize of filing paperwork.

common_wrong_answers.Memorization of Nahj al-Balagha: No, nobody memorized sermons to get tricked onto a bus to Shiraz.
common_wrong_answers.Adhan call competition: Incorrect. He asked them to open the Quran and read.
common_wrong_answers.Ziyarat Ashura recitation: They recited Ziyarat Ashura at night, not to screen typists.

fa.correct_generic: مسابقه قرائت قرآن. کاملاً درسته! برنده شدی که روی مین بروی، اما سر از بایگانی شیراز درآوردی.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، فرمانده مسابقه قرائت قرآن راه انداخت. فریب‌های شیرین جبهه را خوب نخوانده‌اید.

common_wrong_answers.حفظ نهج‌البلاغه: خیر، حفظ خطبه در کار نبود؛ گفت هر کس قرآن را بهتر بخواند جلو بیاید.
common_wrong_answers.مسابقه گفتن اذان: اذان‌گویی نبود؛ متن خاطره به صراحت از روخوانی قرآن می‌گوید.
common_wrong_answers.قرائت زیارت عاشورا: زیارت عاشورا دعای شب عملیات بود، نه ابزار تفکیک نیروهای اداری.

explanation.en: Maryam Alemzadeh recounts an anecdote where an IRGC officer cleverly channeled the troops' religious enthusiasm by staging a fake mine-clearing mission and picking the best Quran readers, only for the proud 'volunteers' to discover they had been selected for administrative duties in Shiraz.
explanation.fa: مریم علم‌زاده خاطره طنزآمیز و معناداری را نقل می‌کند که در آن یک فرمانده برای دور زدن امتناع رزمندگان از انجام امور دفتری، مسابقه قرائت قرآن برای رفتن به میدان مین ترتیب داد و برندگان را سوار اتوبوسِ عازم بایگانی شیراز کرد.

provenance.source_book: British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
provenance.verbatim_passage: [Since there were still too many volunteers] he finally said whoever could read the Quran better would have an advantage. He said and did all this so seriously that nobody suspected. It was only around 2 pm when we were in the bus that we realized we’re headed back to the city and not to a minefield.

clue_text.en: A prominent Iranian opponent of the Pahlavi monarchy who resided in southern Lebanon throughout the 1970s, this Berkeley-educated guerrilla instructor taught Islamic ideology and warfare to Shi'i youth at the Jabal Amil Technical School, deeply mentoring a young Hassan Nasrallah before becoming Iran's post-revolutionary defense minister.
clue_text.fa: این چریک برجسته ایرانی مخالف حکومت پهلوی که در دهه ۱۳۵۰ خورشیدی در جنوب لبنان مستقر بود، در هنرستان فنی جبل عامل به جوانان شیعه از جمله حسن نصرالله جوان آموزش‌های عقیدتی و نظامی داد و پس از انقلاب به وزارت دفاع رسید.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The charismatic Lebanese-Iranian cleric who founded the Amal Movement and invited Chamran to Lebanon.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He was a senior cleric and supreme leader of the Shi'ite community, not a Berkeley-educated defense minister teaching technical school classes.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Iran's ambassador to Damascus in the early 1980s who helped coordinate the founding of Hizbullah.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He served in diplomatic and ministerial posts after the revolution rather than running military-ideological classes at Jabal Amil in 1971.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A radical revolutionary cleric who trained in Palestinian and Lebanese camps during the 1970s.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He led transnational armed liberation brigades rather than serving as the resident teacher and master of Hassan Nasrallah at Jabal Amil.

en.wrong_generic: No. That was Mostafa Chamran. A foundational figure you evidently missed.

explanation.en: Amal Saad cites Hassan Nasrallah's own testimony that Mostafa Chamran was his political and organizational master for two years at the Jabal Amil Art School in Tyre, demonstrating deep pre-revolutionary human ties between Iranian activists and future Lebanese resistance leaders.
explanation.fa: امل سعد با استناد به سخنان سید حسن نصرالله نشان می‌دهد که مصطفی چمران به مدت دو سال در هنرستان فنی جبل عامل در صور استاد تشکیلاتی و سیاسی وی بوده است، امری که پیوندهای انسانی کهن پیش از انقلاب میان فعالان ایرانی و لبنانی را اثبات می‌کند.

provenance.verbatim_passage: Aiding Sadr in the creation of AMAL was another prominent Iranian figure, Mustafa Chamran, a leading opponent of the Pahlavi regime who settled in southern Lebanon in 1971. Chamran spent several years teaching classes in Islamic ideology to devout Shi’ites who would later join AMAL (Chehabi, 2006: 184). One of those students was Nasrallah who studied under Chamran back when he was an AMAL official. According to his account, Chamran left an enduring impact on the Hizbullah leader: 'We used to have weekly or bi-weekly meetings at the Jabal Amil Art [technical] School. Martyr Chamran was our teacher at the school and used to gather the heads of the Amal movement in the South and speak to them … I have to say that in political and organizational terms, Chamran was my master and I enjoyed his teaching for two years'.

clue_text.en: In his book 'Hizbullah: The Story from Within', Deputy Secretary-General Na'im Qasim clarifies that while Hizbullah and the Iranian government share religious devotion to this central Shi'i governing doctrine, the internal administrative machinery of Hizbullah remains completely separate from that of the Iranian state.
clue_text.fa: شیخ نعیم قاسم در کتاب خود با عنوان «حزب‌الله: روایت درونی» تأکید می‌کند که به رغم پایبندی اعتقادی مشترک به این اصل ولایت فقهی، تشکیلات اداری و اجرایی حزب‌الله کاملاً مستقل از نهادهای دولتی ایران فعالیت می‌کند.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The traditional Shi'i institution of source of emulation for religious ritual practice.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Qasim distinguishes individual juristic emulation from the macro-political doctrine of Wilayat al-Faqih which constitutes the movement's foundational mandate.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The internal supreme decision-making executive council of Hizbullah.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It is an internal institutional body within Hizbullah, not the overarching theological-political doctrine.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A well-known anti-colonial diplomatic concept in Iranian foreign policy.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: A secular nationalist foreign policy doctrine associated with Mossadeq, not the Shi'i theocratic governance principle.

en.wrong_generic: No. The doctrine is Wilayat al-Faqih. You mistook a theological compass for municipal government.

fa.wrong_generic: خیر، اصل مورد نظر ولایت فقیه بود. رابطه فقهی را با وابستگی اداری اشتباه گرفته‌اید.

explanation.en: Amal Saad highlights Na'im Qasim's argument that adherence to Wilayat al-Faqih is an intellectual and religious commitment to the Jurisconsult's cosmic authority rather than an administrative subordination to the ministries of the Islamic Republic of Iran.
explanation.fa: امل سعد بر تمایز دقیقی تأکید می‌کند که نعیم قاسم میان تبعیت فقهی از مقام ولی‌فقیه به عنوان رهبر امت و عدم وابستگی به بوروکراسی دولتی ایران قائل شده است.

provenance.verbatim_passage: In his book Hizbullah: The Story from Within, Qasim (2005: 57) elaborates on this distinction: There is no connection between the internal administration of the Iranian state and Hizbullah’s administration. These are two separate issues, each having its particularities and bodies of administration despite the commitment of both to the commands and directions of the Jurist-Theologian who is custodian of the entire nation of Islam and whose power of command is.

clue_text.en: Regarded by scholars as the historical 'Godfather' of Hizbullah, this Iranian ambassador to Syria revealed in an interview that prospective Lebanese fighters gained their early combat experience by volunteering alongside the IRGC inside Iraq during the Iran-Iraq War.
clue_text.fa: این سفیر پیشین ایران در سوریه که در تحلیل‌ها «پدرخوانده» حزب‌الله لقب گرفته است، در مصاحبه‌ای فاش ساخت رزمندگان آینده این تشکل با حضور داوطلبانه در کنار سپاه در جنگ با عراق تجربه رزمی اندوختند.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A key revolutionary diplomat who served as ambassador to Damascus and deputy foreign minister.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He served as ambassador later (1998–2003) and was not the 1982 diplomat hailed as the founding 'Godfather' of Hizbullah.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A prominent career diplomat closely aligned with the Axis of Resistance who served as foreign minister.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Belonged to a much later diplomatic generation and was not involved in the 1982 founding era.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Former foreign minister known for his public debates over the relationship between diplomacy and the battlefield.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He handled multilateral diplomacy in New York and Vienna, completely detached from the 1982 creation of Lebanese resistance factions.

en.wrong_generic: No. The diplomat was Ali Akbar Mohtashemi-Pur. Check your revolutionary embassy records.

explanation.en: Amal Saad cites Ali Akbar Mohtashemi-Pur, Iran's ambassador to Damascus during Hizbullah's founding, who acknowledged that prospective Lebanese fighters gained military competence by fighting alongside Iranian troops during the Iran-Iraq War before returning home.
explanation.fa: امل سعد به اظهارات علی‌اکبر محتشمی‌پور استناد می‌کند که تأیید کرد بخشی از توانایی نظامی حزب‌الله ریشه در حضور داوطلبانه رزمندگان لبنانی در جبهه‌های جنگ ایران و عراق پیش از تأسیس رسمی این جنبش داشته است.

provenance.verbatim_passage: Further demonstrating the flow of support from Lebanon’s Shia to the Islamic Republic was the number of Lebanese fighters who fought alongside the Islamic Revolutionary Guards in the early years of the Iran–Iraq war. As reported by Mohtashemi, who is widely considered Hizbullah’s ‘Godfather’: ‘Part of Hizbullah’s skill goes back to its experience fighting and training … soldiers from Hizbullah fought amongst our troops [in Iraq] or separately’.

clue_text.en: In detailing the pre-revolutionary origins of Lebanese Shi'i institution-building, Saad notes that this Iranian-born cleric arrived in South Lebanon in 1959 to succeed Abdulhusayn Sharafeddin, subsequently creating the Supreme Islamic Shi'ite Council in 1969 and the Movement of the Deprived in 1974.
clue_text.fa: در بررسی ریشه‌های تاریخی تشکل‌یابی شیعیان لبنان، این روحانی ایرانی‌تبار در سال ۱۳۳۸ خورشیدی برای جانشینی سید عبدالحسین شرف‌الدین وارد صور شد و سپس مجلس اعلای شیعیان و جنبش محرومان را تأسیس کرد.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: His prominent cousin in Najaf who authored Iqtisaduna and inspired Islamic movements.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He remained based in Iraq leading the Islamic Da'wa Party until his execution by Saddam Hussein in 1980.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A revered Lebanese Grand Ayatollah often viewed in Western media as Hizbullah's spiritual mentor.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He was an independent jurist based in Beirut who did not found the Supreme Islamic Shi'ite Council or Amal.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The first Secretary-General of Hizbullah from the Bekaa Valley.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He was an early militant leader within Hizbullah before being expelled in 1998, not the 1960s community reformer.

en.wrong_generic: No. The founder was Imam Musa al-Sadr. An elementary piece of Levant history.

explanation.en: Amal Saad documents that Imam Musa al-Sadr, though born and educated in Iran, established the institutional architecture of Lebanese Shi'i empowerment in the 1960s and 1970s, paving the structural groundwork for cadres who later formed Hizbullah.
explanation.fa: امل سعد توضیح می‌دهد که امام موسی صدر با تأسیس مجلس اعلای شیعیان و جنبش امل، جایگاه اجتماعی و سیاسی شیعیان لبنان را متحول کرد و زمینه پیوستن نسل اول کادرهای آن به تشکیلات حزب‌الله را فراهم ساخت.

provenance.verbatim_passage: Muhammad Baqr as-Sadr’s cousin, Musa as-Sadr, who, though of Lebanese ancestry, was born and raised in Iran. On the request of local community leaders, Sadr took up an invitation to succeed Sayyid Abdulhusayn Sharafeddin as religious leader of South Lebanon’s Shi’ites in 1959. In light of the Lebanese government’s neglect of the Shi’ite community’s socioeconomic, political and security concerns, Sadr pressed for the establishment of institutions to redress these grievances – the Supreme Islamic Shi’ite Council in 1969 and Council of the South in 1970. Sadr also played a critical role in politicising the Lebanese Shi’ites through the vehicle of the Ashura commemorations. These efforts culminated in his creation of the Movement of the Deprived in 1974 and its military adjunct, the AMAL movement in 1975.

clue_text.en: According to Amal Saad's archival documentation, Hizbullah's structural emergence in 1982 was coordinated by this specific consultative body of Lebanese clerical and lay militants, which sent an official delegation to Tehran to solicit Ayatollah Khomeini's formal religious authorization.
clue_text.fa: به استناد شواهد پژوهشی امل سعد، اعلام موجودیت ساختاری حزب‌الله در سال ۱۳۶۱ توسط این شورای مشورتی نه نفره متشکل از روحانیون و چریک‌های لبنانی هماهنگ شد که هیئتی را برای اخذ اجازه شرعی به نزد آیت‌الله خمینی فرستادند.

en: Committee Supportive of the Islamic Revolution

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A cultural group established in Lebanon in 1979 whose members formed Hizbullah's initial nucleus.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It was the earlier 1979 cultural society, whereas the 1982 founding body that dispatched the delegation to Khomeini was the Committee of Nine.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A title resembling formal Shi'i clerical governing councils.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: No such formal organ existed; the foundational body coordinating between Amal, Da'wa, and independent clerics was the Committee of Nine.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A key pro-revolutionary clerical body in Lebanon uniting Sunni and Shi'i clerics.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: While its clerics participated in discussions, it was not the specific 9-member executive committee that created Hizbullah.

en.correct_generic: Committee of Nine. Impressive. You actually know the archival origin story.
en.wrong_generic: No. The founding body was the Committee of Nine. Not something you pick up from cable news.

common_wrong_answers.Supreme Leadership Council: Inventing formal titles won't fool anyone here.

explanation.en: Amal Saad documents that the 'Committee of Nine' (comprising representatives from Amal, the Islamic Da'wa Party, and independent scholars) served as Hizbullah's transitional founding council, sending a delegation to obtain Ayatollah Khomeini's approval as Wali al-Faqih.
explanation.fa: امل سعد توضیح می‌دهد که «کمیته نه نفره» متشکل از نمایندگان احزاب امل، الدعوه و علمای مستقل، به عنوان هسته مؤسس حزب‌الله هیئتی را برای کسب مشروعیت فقهی و اجازه تأسیس نزد آیت‌الله خمینی اعزام کرد.

provenance.verbatim_passage: As detailed in the preceding section, the ‘Committee of Nine’ dispatched a delegation to obtain the Wilayat al-Faqih’s religious legal approval for the establishment of Hizbullah. While the Islamic resistance’s agenda coincided with the Faqih’s ruling on the obligation to fight Israel, Hizbullah’s founding was predicated on this authorization.

clue_text.en: In his classic theoretical model of proxy intervention, Swedish scholar Bertil Dunér argues that neither material assistance nor shared ideology is a sufficient condition to establish a proxy relationship; instead, the defining criterion is the sponsor's exercise of this coercive form of power.
clue_text.fa: در نظریه تحلیلی برتیل دونر درباره جنگ‌های نیابتی، نه کمک‌های مادی و نه اشتراک ایدئولوژیک هیچ‌کدام برای تحقق رابطه نیابتی کافی نیستند، بلکه معیار اصلی اعمال این شکل از قدرت قهرآمیز برای واداشتن گروه به مداخله است.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Material and financial transfers are commonly assumed by realists to buy subservience.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Dunér specifically demonstrates that receiving material aid without coercive pressure does not constitute a proxy relationship.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The ideational alignment that constructivists highlight as creating shared worldview.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Shared norms create solidarity and comradeship rather than the subordination demanded by proxy theories.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A key sovereign benefit states extend to allied non-state actors.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Diplomatic backing is an external legitimation tool, completely distinct from Dunér's core criterion of coercive power.

specificity_prompt.en: Please identify the specific coercive mechanism required in Dunér's proxy definition.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً اصطلاح دقیق دونر در خصوص اِعمال قدرت قهرآمیز را بیان کنید.

en.correct_generic: Compulsion. Exactly. If nobody forced you into the fight, you are an ally, not a proxy.
en.wrong_generic: No. Dunér's threshold was compulsion. Money alone does not make an obedient puppet.

common_wrong_answers.Financial Subsidization: Dunér explicitly rejects aid as sufficient. You cannot simply buy a proxy status.
common_wrong_answers.Ideological Socialization: Socialization creates friends and believers, not coerced proxies.
common_wrong_answers.Diplomatic Recognition: Recognition is a diplomatic handshake, not military compulsion.

fa.correct_generic: اجبار. کاملاً درسته! وقتی با زور وارد جنگ نشده باشی، متحدی نه دست‌نشانده.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست اجبار بود. نظریه دونر را سرسری خوانده‌اید.

common_wrong_answers.تأمین مالی: دونر صراحتاً کمک مالی را شرط کافی نمی‌داند؛ پول بدون زور نیابت نمی‌آورد.
common_wrong_answers.جامعه‌پذیری ایدئولوژیک: جامعه‌پذیری همبستگی می‌آورد، نه اجبار و سلطه نیابتی.
common_wrong_answers.شناسایی دیپلماتیک: شناسایی سیاسی ابزار مشروعیت است، نه فشار قهرآمیز نظامی.

explanation.en: Amal Saad uses Bertil Dunér's criteria to demonstrate that because Iran does not compel or pressure Hizbullah into interventions against its own strategic interests, the relationship fails the theoretical definition of a sponsor-proxy hierarchy.
explanation.fa: امل سعد با اتکا به نظریه برتیل دونر نشان می‌دهد از آنجا که ایران حزب‌الله را تحت فشار قهرآمیز برای مداخله قرار نمی‌دهد، اطلاق عنوان دست‌نشانده یا نیروی نیابتی از نظر علمی فاقد وجاهت است.

provenance.verbatim_passage: Although Dunér’s proxy model examines material support and compatibility of interest as variables, he neither views them as necessary nor sufficient conditions for the proxy status. For him, the ‘exercise of power’ is the paramount determinant of a proxy relationship, where power is understood strictly as ‘compulsion’... As such, an actor who receives material support but is not pressured to intervene is not a proxy.

clue_text.en: Highlighting Hizbullah's operational autonomy during the Syrian Civil War, an Iraqi militia commander interviewed by Reuters noted that while Iranian officers closely directed all other foreign Shi'i factions, Hizbullah uniquely maintained this status.
clue_text.fa: در اثبات استقلال عملیاتی حزب‌الله در بحران سوریه، یک فرمانده شبه‌نظامی عراقی در مصاحبه با رویترز اذعان کرد که فرماندهان ایرانی همه گروه‌ها را اداره می‌کنند اما حزب‌الله از این وضعیت ممتاز برخوردار است.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The standard media framing that Hizbullah followed direct Iranian battlefield commands.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The commander's exact quote explicitly contrasts Hizbullah's stand-alone status with other subservient groups.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Reflects joint operations between Syrian, Russian, and Iranian military headquarters.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Hizbullah maintained separate operational command, compelling even Iranian officers to coordinate with them as equals.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Iran often officially characterized its military deployment in Syria as purely advisory.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Hizbullah deployed front-line assault battalions and commanded local battlefields rather than merely advising.

specificity_prompt.en: Please state the exact descriptor used by the Iraqi commander regarding Hizbullah's command status.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً واژه دقیقی را که فرمانده عراقی در مصاحبه برای توصیف حزب‌الله به کار برد بیان کنید.

en.correct_generic: Independent. Quite right. 'The Iranians manage all the factions, but Hezbollah is independent'.
en.wrong_generic: No. The word was 'independent'. Even their fellow Shi'i militias acknowledged the hierarchy.

common_wrong_answers.Subordinate: Completely wrong. The quote explicitly denied they were subordinate.
common_wrong_answers.Integrated: They fought alongside each other, but Hizbullah ran its own show.
common_wrong_answers.Advisory: Hizbullah took the casualties on the frontlines; that is hardly an advisory role.

fa.correct_generic: مستقل. کاملاً درسته! همان تعبیر رویترز که گفت ایرانی‌ها همه را اداره می‌کنند اما حزب‌الله مستقل است.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست مستقل بود. حتی نیروهای عراقی هم به استقلال حزب‌الله اذعان داشتند.

common_wrong_answers.تحت امر: کاملاً برعکس؛ متن صریحاً می‌گوید برخلاف سایرین تحت امر نبودند.
common_wrong_answers.ادغام‌شده: آن‌ها در اتاق‌های عملیاتی دوشادوش هم بودند اما استقلال رزمی حزب‌الله حفظ شد.
common_wrong_answers.مشاوره‌ای: حزب‌الله خط‌شکن نبردها بود، نه هیئت مستشاری پشت جبهه.

explanation.en: Amal Saad cites battlefield reporting from Syria where allied commanders confirmed that Hizbullah acted as an autonomous military peer rather than a subordinate faction managed by Iranian officers.
explanation.fa: امل سعد به گزارش‌های میدانی رویترز استناد می‌کند که در آن فرماندهان محور مقاومت تأیید کرده‌اند حزب‌الله در سوریه در جایگاه یک نیروی هم‌تراز و مستقل عمل می‌کرد نه یک گروه وابسته به فرماندهان ایرانی.

provenance.verbatim_passage: is echoed by an Iraqi commander in Syria, interviewed by Reuters, who admitted that Hizbullah enjoyed much more autonomy than other foreign Shia fighters in Syria: ‘The Iranians manage all the factions but Hezbollah is independent’ (Perry et al, 2016). Hizbullah’s independence can be further ascertained by the fact that it was the movement that convinced Iran of the need to intervene in Syria, rather than the other way around.

clue_text.en: In challenging Cold War proxy assumptions, Bertil Dunér highlights that this Caribbean island nation was erroneously categorized as a Soviet proxy during its military intervention in the Angolan Civil War, when it actually acted out of Third World anti-colonial affinity.
clue_text.fa: برتیل دونر در نقد پیش‌فرض‌های جنگ سرد نشان می‌دهد که این کشور جزیره‌ای حوزه کارائیب در مداخله نظامی خود در جنگ داخلی آنگولا به غلط دست‌نشانده شوروی خوانده شد، در حالی که انگیزه‌های استعمارستیزانه خود را دنبال می‌کرد.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A Latin American revolutionary state aligned with the Soviet bloc during the 1980s.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The Sandinistas fought domestic Contras and did not dispatch tens of thousands of troops to southern Africa.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A Soviet-backed socialist state that intervened militarily in neighboring Cambodia in 1978.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Intervened in Southeast Asia to overthrow the Khmer Rouge, not in the African theater in Angola.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A heavily militarized non-aligned state known for sending technical and military advisors to African regimes.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Never deployed combat expeditionary corps to fight South African forces in Angola like Havana did.

specificity_prompt.en: Please name the Caribbean socialist country analyzed by Dunér.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً نام این کشور سوسیالیستی حوزه دریای کارائیب را بیان کنید.

en.correct_generic: Cuba. Yes. Castro sent troops to Angola long before Moscow knew what to do with them.
en.wrong_generic: No. The country was Cuba. Even standard Cold War history seems to elude you.

common_wrong_answers.Nicaragua: Nicaragua was defending Managua, not sending divisions to southern Africa.
common_wrong_answers.Vietnam: Vietnam invaded Cambodia, not Angola. Check your hemispheres.
common_wrong_answers.North Korea: North Korea provided tunnels and pilots, not tens of thousands of ground troops in Luanda.

fa.correct_generic: کوبا. کاملاً درسته! فیدل کاسترو پیش از آنکه مسکو تصمیم بگیرد، نیروهایش را به آنگولا فرستاده بود.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، کشور مورد نظر کوبا بود. تاریخ جنگ سرد را با حدس زدن نمی‌شود پاس کرد.

common_wrong_answers.نیکاراگوئه: ساندینیست‌های نیکاراگوئه درگیر کنتراها در مرز خود بودند، نه اعزام ارتش به آفریقا.
common_wrong_answers.ویتنام: ویتنام وارد کامبوج شد نه آنگولا؛ قاره‌ها را اشتباه گرفتید.
common_wrong_answers.کره شمالی: کره شمالی کارشناس نظامی می‌فرستاد، نه لشکرهای پیاده‌نظام به جنگ داخلی آنگولا.

explanation.en: Amal Saad cites Dunér's analysis of Cuba's intervention in Angola as a historical parallel to Hizbullah in Syria: junior allies frequently take autonomous, high-risk military initiatives driven by shared ideological affinity rather than great power dictation.
explanation.fa: امل سعد به بررسی تاریخی دونر از مداخله مستقل کوبا در آنگولا استناد می‌کند تا نشان دهد چگونه متحدان کوچک‌تر بر پایه آرمان‌های مشترک، مستقل از اراده ابرقدرت‌ها دست به مداخلات فرامرزی می‌زنند.

provenance.verbatim_passage: To argue that subordination and ideological allegiance are not mutually exclusive concepts is to belittle the social and political bonds generated by collectively-held norms, and to underestimate the socialising impact of a shared worldview, which obviates the need for political control. Dunér (1981: 354–5) is an exception among proxy theorists; he argues that Cuba was mislabelled a proxy of the Soviet Union’s, while attributing its intervention in Angola to ‘its long history of affinity with the Third World’ and to a convergence of objectives between it and its superpower ‘ally’.

clue_text.en: In an August 2017 victory speech cited by Saad as evidence of Hizbullah's elevated regional standing, Syrian President Bashar al-Assad explicitly placed Sayyid Hassan Nasrallah alongside President Vladimir Putin and this Iranian Supreme Leader as the tripartite authors of regional triumph.
clue_text.fa: در سخنرانی پیروزی مرداد ۱۳۹۶ که به عنوان سندی بر ارتقای جایگاه منطقه‌ای حزب‌الله ذکر شده، بشار اسد نام حسن نصرالله را در کنار ولادیمیر پوتین و این رهبر عالی ایران به عنوان سه ضلع پیروزی قرار داد.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The famed commander of the IRGC Quds Force who spearheaded military operations across Syria.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Assad's official address specifically named the heads of state and movements (Khamenei, Putin, and Nasrallah), not military commanders.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The sitting President of the Islamic Republic of Iran during the August 2017 speech.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Assad praised 'Imam Khamenei' as the sovereign supreme leader rather than the civilian president.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council coordinating regional military strategy.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Assad invoked the highest ideological and state authority of the Islamic Republic, not security secretaries.

specificity_prompt.en: Please specify the Iranian Supreme Leader praised by Assad in his 2017 speech.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً نام رهبر جمهوری اسلامی ایران که اسد در نطق خود از او تجلیل کرد را بیان کنید.

en.correct_generic: Ali Khamenei. Correct. A diplomatic shout-out that placed a guerrilla leader on par with heads of state.
en.wrong_generic: No. Assad named Ali Khamenei alongside Putin and Nasrallah. Check the speech transcript.

common_wrong_answers.Qasem Soleimani: Assad named the political sovereigns, not the battlefield generals.
common_wrong_answers.Hassan Rouhani: Rouhani was never given credit for the Syrian military campaign.
common_wrong_answers.Ali Shamkhani: Shamkhani ran security councils, not the ideological axis.

fa.correct_generic: سید علی خامنه‌ای. کاملاً درسته! نطقی که رهبر یک جنبش را هم‌ردیف سران دو کشور بزرگ قرار داد.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، بشار اسد از آیت‌الله خامنه‌ای نام برد. متن سخنرانی‌های دمشق را دقیق نخوانده‌اید.

common_wrong_answers.قاسم سلیمانی: اسد رهبران عالی سه ضلع را نام برد، نه فرماندهان میدان نبرد را.
common_wrong_answers.حسن روحانی: دولت روحانی در دمشق کاره‌ای نبود که اسد از او تجلیل کند.
common_wrong_answers.علی شمخانی: شمخانی هماهنگ‌کننده امنیتی بود، نه رهبر معنوی و سیاسی محور.

explanation.en: Amal Saad emphasizes that Bashar al-Assad's 2017 speech formally treated Hizbullah as an equal regional power alongside Russia and Iran, disproving Western depictions of the movement as merely a disposable proxy.
explanation.fa: امل سعد تأکید می‌کند که نطق سال ۲۰۱۷ بشار اسد و تجلیل هم‌ردیف از پوتین، رهبر ایران و نصرالله، نشان‌دهنده ارتقای حزب‌الله به تراز یک قدرت منطقه‌ای هم‌پیمان است نه یک نیروی نیابتی دست‌نشانده.

provenance.verbatim_passage: Assad (2017) goes even further, not only paying tribute to Hizbullah’s fighters for defending Syria, but elevating the movement to the same rank as major powers like Russia and regional powers like Iran: 'As the Syrian Arab people along with the armed forces write down a new history for Syria and the region today, chapters will be written about Iran and Imam Khamenei, about Russia and President Putin, and about Hizbullah and Sayyid Hasan Nasrallah'.

clue_text.en: Illustrating that reciprocal solidarity predated the Islamic Republic's founding, Amal Saad notes that in early 1979, before the Pahlavi regime's sudden collapse obviated the mission, this exact number of Lebanese AMAL fighters volunteered to travel to Iran to fight alongside revolutionary insurgents.
clue_text.fa: در اثبات همبستگی متقابل پیش از پیروزی انقلاب، امل سعد اشاره می‌کند که در اوایل سال ۱۳۵۷ پیش از سقوط غیرمنتظره رژیم پهلوی، این تعداد دقیق از رزمندگان جنبش امل برای نبرد مسلحانه در کنار انقلابیون عازم ایران شده بودند.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The approximate size of early IRGC contingent trainers dispatched to Lebanon in 1982.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Reflects the later 1982 training detachments in Baalbek rather than the 1979 Lebanese volunteers.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A common rough round figure cited for mobilization brigades.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Houshang Chehabi's archival records cited by Saad confirm the exact number of volunteers was 500.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The typical company strength of specialized commando units.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Substantially underestimates the 500 fighters ready to deploy.

specificity_prompt.en: Please specify the exact number of AMAL volunteer fighters recorded in the historical literature.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً رقم دقیق نیروهای داوطلب امل را مطابق اسناد تاریخی ذکر کنید.

en.correct_generic: 500. Correct. An archival number you actually managed to recall. Don't get arrogant.
en.wrong_generic: No. The recorded number was 500. Guessing round numbers won't rescue you here.

common_wrong_answers.200: 200 was the Pasdaran contingent sent to Baalbek in 1982, not the 1979 AMAL volunteers.
common_wrong_answers.1,000: Exaggerating by double won't earn you points. It was 500.
common_wrong_answers.150: Way too low. 500 fighters were ready to deploy to Tehran.

fa.correct_generic: ۵۰۰ نفر. کاملاً درسته! معلوم است پاورقی‌های تاریخی را بادقت خوانده‌اید.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، آمار ثبت‌شده ۵۰۰ نفر بود. پرتاب اعداد شانسی کمکی به شما نمی‌کند.

common_wrong_answers.۲۰۰ نفر: ۲۰۰ نفر تعداد پاسداران اعزامی به بعلبک در سال ۱۳۶۱ بود، نه چریک‌های امل در سال ۱۳۵۷.
common_wrong_answers.۱۰۰۰ نفر: بزرگ‌نمایی دو برابری به کارتان نمی‌آید؛ آمار دقیق ۵۰۰ نفر بود.
common_wrong_answers.۱۵۰ نفر: بسیار کمتر از واقعیت؛ ۵۰۰ رزمنده داوطلب اعزام به ایران بودند.

explanation.en: Citing historical research by Houchang Chehabi, Amal Saad points out that 500 Lebanese AMAL fighters volunteered to defend the nascent Iranian Revolution in early 1979, proving that military solidarity flowed bidirectionally rather than as a top-down creation of Tehran.
explanation.fa: امل سعد با استناد به پژوهش هوشنگ شهابی خاطرنشان می‌سازد که ۵۰۰ رزمنده داوطلب جنبش امل در آستانه پیروزی انقلاب برای کمک به انقلابیون اعلام آمادگی کردند، امری که دوطرفه بودن پیوندهای مقاومت را پیش از تأسیس جمهوری اسلامی نشان می‌دهد.

provenance.verbatim_passage: The collaborative nature of this relationship was also evinced by the 500 AMAL fighters who volunteered to go and fight alongside the revolutionaries, although the hasty collapse of the Shah’s regime obviated the need for their participation in the fighting (Chehabi, 2006: 203).

category.en: THE WHEELS ON THE BUS GO HALAL

clue_text.en: In the early revolutionary decade of the 1980s, Tehran's public bus company replaced the terms 'men and women' with these two familial, revolutionary labels to designate the passengers separated by newly installed metal bars.
clue_text.fa: در نخستین دهه پس از پیروزی انقلاب، شرکت واحد اتوبوسرانی تهران به جای واژگان «مردان و زنان»، این دو عنوان خویشاوندی و انقلابی را برای تفکیک مسافران دو سوی میله‌های فلزی به کار برد.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Reflects the leftist and secular revolutionary vocabulary common in 1979 before clerical consolidation.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The Islamic Republic denounced Marxist terms like 'comrades' in favor of Islamic familial designations.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Represents traditional patriarchal and maternal family values often extolled in cultural rhetoric.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Public spaces were divided along horizontal generational bonds of fraternity and sorority rather than parental titles.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The historical national emblem of pre-revolutionary Iran that appeared on public transit and charity societies.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Monarchical symbols were immediately purged from state infrastructure after February 1979.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the exact familial titles used to designate male and female bus riders in early post-revolutionary Iran.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً عناوین دقیق خویشاوندی و انقلابی به کار رفته برای خطاب مسافران زن و مرد را ذکر فرمایید.

en.correct_generic: Sisters and Brothers. Quite right. Even your uncle on the city bus remembers that decree.
en.wrong_generic: No. The terms were Sisters and Brothers. A standard staple of revolutionary bureaucracy.

common_wrong_answers.Comrades and Citizens: Comrades? This was Tehran in the 1980s, not Leningrad in 1917.
common_wrong_answers.Fathers and Mothers: No. They weren't checking birth certificates for parenthood at the bus turnstile.
common_wrong_answers.Lions and Sun: Wrong regime. The monarchy's lions had already been scrubbed off the paintwork.

fa.correct_generic: خواهران و برادران. کاملاً درسته! بالاخره ابتدایی‌ترین واژگان خط واحد دهه شصت را به یاد آوردید.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، عناوین رسمی خواهران و برادران بود. حتی اعلامیه‌های شرکت واحد را هم نخوانده‌اید.

common_wrong_answers.رفقا و شهروندان: رفقا؟ اشتباه آمدید؛ اینجا تهران بعد از انقلاب بود، نه مسکو.
common_wrong_answers.پدران و مادران: خیر، قرار نبود بر اساس شناسنامه خانوادگی سوار اتوبوس شوند.
common_wrong_answers.شیران و خورشید: نشان شیر و خورشید در همان بهمن پنجاه و هفت از در و دیوار پاک شد.

explanation.en: Nazanin Shahrokni demonstrates that during the 1980s, the Bus Company of Tehran partitioned buses between 'sisters' and 'brothers' rather than 'women' and 'men,' reflecting the pervasive adoption of an Islamic and revolutionary ethics across municipal infrastructure.
explanation.fa: نازنین شاهرکنی در پژوهش خود نشان می‌دهد که در دهه شصت خورشیدی، شرکت واحد اتوبوسرانی تهران به جای اصطلاحات متداول زنان و مردان، تعابیر خواهران و برادران را به کار بست تا اخلاق و نظم انقلابی و اسلامی را بر فضاهای حرکتی شهر مسلط کند.

provenance.source_book: Women in Place: The Politics of Gender Segregation in Iran
provenance.verbatim_passage: The 1980s were the years of the double-decker buses, giant ship-like, blue and orange buses with two floors. Gender segregation on these buses was easy, or so it seemed; the first floor was assigned to 'sisters' and the second floor to 'brothers.' The use of 'sisters' and 'brothers' as opposed to 'women' and 'men' points to the dominance of an Islamic and a revolutionary discourse and ethics.

category.en: THE WHEELS ON THE BUS GO HALAL

clue_text.en: During the 1980s, municipal planners initially tested gender segregation on these iconic, two-floor blue and orange vehicles by dedicating the lower deck to women and the upper deck to men before empty seats forced a repartition.
clue_text.fa: در دهه ۱۳۶۰ خورشیدی، مدیران شهری تفکیک جنسیتی را ابتدا در این وسایل نقلیه عمومی دوطبقه آبی و نارنجی آزمایش کردند و طبقه اول را به زنان و طبقه دوم را به مردان اختصاص دادند.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A prominent mass-transit system that later reconfigured bus gender segregation in Tehran.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: BRT buses were imported and introduced decades later in 2007, not during the 1980s wartime era.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Widely used across Iranian cities for suburban commuting and local transit lines.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Minivans possess single small cabins without vertical decks and were not the massive two-floor vehicles analyzed by Shahrokni.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Tehran's metro system features strict gender segregation with designated end-of-train women's cars.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The Tehran underground metro did not begin commercial passenger operations until the late 1990s.

specificity_prompt.en: Please name the specific type of two-story bus operated in Tehran during the 1980s.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً نوع مشخص این اتوبوس‌های شهری دو اشکوبه مورد استفاده در دهه شصت را نام ببرید.

en.correct_generic: Double-decker buses. Correct. A brief moment of clarity before you inevitably miss the next one.
en.wrong_generic: Incorrect. We were looking for double-decker buses. Giant blue and orange leviathans.

common_wrong_answers.BRT bendy buses: BRT arrived in 2007 under Ghalibaf. Try to keep your centuries straight.
common_wrong_answers.Private minivans: Minivans do not have a second floor. Basic physics eludes you.
common_wrong_answers.Subway metro cars: The metro was still a flooded construction ditch in the 1980s.

fa.correct_generic: اتوبوس‌های دوطبقه. کاملاً درسته! غول‌های آبی و نارنجی که بالاخره مسافران را تقسیم کردند.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست اتوبوس‌های دوطبقه بود. این سازه‌های متحرک را همه دیده‌اند.

common_wrong_answers.اتوبوس‌های تندرو: اتوبوس‌های تندرو محصول سال ۱۳۸۶ و شهرداری قالیباف بود، نه دهه شصت.
common_wrong_answers.مینی‌بوس‌های خصوصی: مینی‌بوس طبقه دوم ندارد؛ کمترین دقتی در خواندن صورت سوال به خرج ندادید.
common_wrong_answers.واگن‌های مترو: متروی تهران در دهه شصت صرفاً یک طرح معلق و حفر تونل نیمه‌کاره بود.

explanation.en: Shahrokni documents that the Bus Company of Tehran initially sought an effortless solution to segregation by assigning the first deck of double-decker buses to women and the second to men; however, because the first floor remained underutilized while the second overflowed, the company installed movable metal partitions on the lower deck.
explanation.fa: شاهرکنی تشریح می‌کند که شرکت واحد ابتدا طبقه اول اتوبوس‌های دوطبقه را به زنان و طبقه دوم را به مردان اختصاص داد، اما خالی ماندن بخشی از طبقه پایین و هجوم مردان به طبقه بالا، مدیران را وادار کرد تا با نصب میله‌های متحرک در طبقه اول سهم زنان را به یک‌سوم کاهش دهند.

provenance.source_book: Women in Place: The Politics of Gender Segregation in Iran
provenance.verbatim_passage: The 1980s were the years of the double-decker buses, giant ship-like, blue and orange buses with two floors. Gender segregation on these buses was easy, or so it seemed; the first floor was assigned to 'sisters' and the second floor to 'brothers.' But as the giant bus traversed the city, its first floor remained partially empty. 'Brothers' were crowded on the second floor, while there were not that many 'sisters' to fill in the first-floor space.

category.en: THE WHEELS ON THE BUS GO HALAL

clue_text.en: Introduced in 2007 under Mayor Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf following a municipal mission to Colombia, this high-speed bus transit network inverted decades of domestic convention by seating women in the front cabin and men in the rear.
clue_text.fa: این سامانه ترابری که در سال ۱۳۸۶ خورشیدی پس از بازدید هیئت شهرداری تهران از کلمبیا راه‌اندازی شد، برخلاف عرف پیشین، کابین جلو را به زنان و بخش عقب را به مردان اختصاص داد.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A highly contested transit initiative championed by Mahmoud Ahmadinejad during his mayoral tenure.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The monorail project in Sadeghiyeh was abandoned as unviable and never launched as a functioning transit network.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Reflects Tehran's women-only private taxi service launched with female drivers in 2006.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It was a fleet of private green passenger sedans, not the dedicated rapid transit bus network modeled on Bogota.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A major component of Tehran's intermediate transport system regulated by municipal authorities.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Vans operate without segregated cabins or dedicated corridors and did not invert front-rear gender allocations.

specificity_prompt.en: Please provide the common acronym or full name of Tehran's rapid bus system launched in 2007.
specificity_prompt.fa: لطفاً نام یا سرواژه مصطلح این سامانه اتوبوسرانی پرسرعت احداث شده در سال ۱۳۸۶ را بنویسید.

en.correct_generic: Bus Rapid Transit. Correct. Front seats for the sisters, diesel fumes for the brothers.
en.wrong_generic: No. The system is the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT). Have you ever set foot on Valiasr Street?

common_wrong_answers.Tehran Monorail: Ahmadinejad's monorail pillars were demolished before a single passenger bought a token.
common_wrong_answers.Green Taxi Fleet: Taxis don't run in dedicated segregated red lanes with articulated accordion joints.
common_wrong_answers.Shared Van Shuttles: No. Van passengers sit shoulder-to-shoulder whether they like it or not.

fa.correct_generic: اتوبوس‌های تندرو. کاملاً درسته! همان خطوط بی‌آرتی که جای زن و مرد را در اتوبوس برعکس کرد.
fa.wrong_generic: خیر، پاسخ درست خطوط بی‌آرتی (اتوبوس‌های تندرو) بود. خیابان ولی‌عصر را ندیده‌اید؟

common_wrong_answers.مونوریل تهران: پایه‌های مونوریل صادقیه را هم که سال‌ها پیش جمع کردند و رفتند.
common_wrong_answers.تاکسیرانی سبز: تاکسی‌های بانوان سمند و پراید بودند، نه خطوط ویژه اتوبوسرانی شهری.
common_wrong_answers.ونکارهای خطی: در ون‌های خطی زن و مرد فشرده کنار هم می‌نشینند و خبری از کابین جدا نیست.

explanation.en: Shahrokni explains that Tehran's BRT network, adopted from Bogota's TransMilenio in 2007, inverted the classic bus segregation pattern by seating women in the front cabin and men in the rear, reflecting women's transformation from marginalized riders into valued public consumers.
explanation.fa: شاهرکنی تشریح می‌کند که راه‌اندازی خطوط بی‌آرتی در سال ۱۳۸۶ با الگوبرداری از ترانسمیلنیوی بوگوتا، چینش سنتی تفکیک را معکوس کرد؛ به طوری که زنان برای سوار و پیاده شدن راحت‌تر به کابین جلو منتقل شدند تا نقش آنان از مسافران حاشیه‌ای به مصرف‌کنندگان محترم شهری بازتعریف شود.

provenance.source_book: Women in Place: The Politics of Gender Segregation in Iran
provenance.verbatim_passage: The privatization plan was complemented by Bus Rapid Transit, a high-quality, bus-based transit system that delivers fast and comfortable services. Introduced in Tehran in 2007 after municipal officials visited the TransMilenio BRT operation in Bogota, Colombia, the BRT lines generated much controversy. First of all, the BCT reintroduced the concept of women-only buses, intended to provide female passengers with more space and safety.

category.en: THE WHEELS ON THE BUS GO HALAL

clue_text.en: In the mid-1990s, letters published in Zan-e Rooz complained that male passengers routinely usurped the two women-only rows on the heavily overcrowded bus route connecting Valiasr Square to this all-female university.
clue_text.fa: در اواسط دهه ۱۳۷۰ خورشیدی، نامه‌های اعتراضی زنان در مجله زن روز نشان داد که مسافران مرد در ساعات شلوغی صندلی‌های اندک زنان را در مسیر منتهی به این دانشگاه ویژه بانوان اشغال می‌کردند.
